Conservative and Non-Conservative Forces:

A force is said to be conservative if the total work done by it on moving a particle roun a closed path is zero. The work done by it in moving a particle from one point to another point depends only on the distance between these points but not the actual path followed. For example, gravitational forcev A force is said to be non-conservative if the work done by it on moving a particle round a closed path is not zero. The work done by non-conservative force depends upon the path followed and initial and final position also. For example, frictional force.
